value: stable minus 2 minor versions, raised only in a minor release, declared as rust-version in Cargo.toml and tested in CI

logging-pipeline/v1: STACK - tracing 0.1.44 is the only diagnostic facade any package may name, taken default-features = false, features = ["std"] by rs-launch-blueprint-core and rs-launch-blueprint-web and with its defaults (std, attributes) by the root package rs-launch-blueprint and rs-launch-blueprint-cli; tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 with features = ["env-filter"] over its default set (smallvec, fmt, ansi, tracing-log, std) is declared on the root package only, with the json feature OFF because the template owns the structured formatter and the feature adds exactly two crates (serde, tracing-serde) for a formatter it replaces, and with local-time NEVER enabled because the crate's own documentation says the local-offset lookup may be unsound or fail; timestamps are UTC ISO-8601; tracing-log 0.2.0 enters through tracing-subscriber's default tracing-log feature and is never declared directly; no other logging crate is added; crates/core, crates/cli and crates/web must not name tracing-subscriber, enforced by R02's cargo deny --all-features check bans [bans] deny[].wrappers rule and its crates/core allow-list test; the version floor is 0.3.20, RUSTSEC-2025-0055's patched floor. INITIALISATION - exactly one telemetry::init(Profile) -> Init in the root package's src/telemetry.rs, called first in each binary's main before anything that can log; it builds Registry::default() with a reload::Layer<EnvFilter> and one fmt layer whose writer is stderr, and first checks tracing::dispatcher::has_been_set(): if a dispatcher is already set, a host owns diagnostics, nothing is installed and init returns Init::HostOwned; otherwise it installs with SubscriberInitExt::try_init() and NEVER init(), which is try_init().expect(..), returning Init::Installed(Handles { level: reload::Handle<EnvFilter, Registry>, log_bridge_refused: false }) on Ok and Init::Installed(Handles { level, log_bridge_refused: true }) on Err, because try_init sets the global dispatcher before it installs the log bridge, so an Err after a clear check means only that a host already owns the log logger while the template's dispatcher is live; init never panics, never replaces and never tears down anything; template code never calls tracing_log::LogTracer::init(), because try_init already installs the bridge with the subscriber's max-level hint and a second installation fails with SetLoggerError; tests and embedders use the scoped set_default guard instead of the global path. RECONFIGURATION - the level is swappable after the configuration file is read, through the returned reload::Handle, which is how F274's config tier is reached without logging being absent while the configuration file is parsed; the format and the writer are fixed at init and are not reloadable, a deliberate departure from py's handler-replacement model recorded as a migration risk. STRUCTURED-FIELD AND REDACTION CONTRACT - key-based masking is applied at format time, not event time, because a tracing::Event is immutable, RecordFields is a sealed trait and no Layer can rewrite an event; the key vocabulary is F252's verbatim (token, password, secret, authorization, api_key, apikey, credential, cookie, matched as an ASCII-lowercased substring) and the mask is [REDACTED]; the human profile uses a template-owned FormatFields wrapping DefaultFields, and the structured profile uses a template-owned FormatEvent plus a template-owned JSON FormatFields, because tracing-subscriber's stock Format<Json> serialises event fields itself through tracing_serde in both its flattened and non-flattened branches and uses its N: FormatFields parameter only for span fields, so a redacting field formatter under .json() leaks every event field and panics if its output is not valid JSON; secrecy::SecretString (R56 revision 2) is the type-level first line of defence and the key match is the second; the structured line's key order is level, target, the R78 trace-correlation slot, the event's own fields, then span; the HTTP correlation field is named request_id, matching CLI Design Standard R7.8's spelling, while the wire header stays request-id per REST API Design Standard R11.7 and section 1.10; redaction is a property of rendered output, so any later exporter layer must apply the policy itself; and the residual gap - a secret carried inside a non-sensitive field's value is not masked - is recorded as OVERRIDE (OV-09) against CLI Design Standard R5.6. PROFILES (one engine, two policies; one subscriber per process, since each front end is its own binary) - Profile::Cli for the CLI binary R49 names: format auto, console or json, where auto resolves to console when std::io::stderr().is_terminal() and to json otherwise, colour from R65's resolved anstream::ColorChoice passed to .with_ansi(bool), default level WARN; Profile::Service { level, format } for the serve binary R69 gates: format from RSLBP_WEB_LOG_FORMAT, whose value set is json (the default) or console with no auto and no TTY test, any other value rejected by the FromStr R77's WebSettings::from_env() calls as R67's RSLB203 before init runs; default level INFO; no file sink; level and format are the values R77's WebSettings::from_env() parsed from RSLBP_WEB_LOG_LEVEL and RSLBP_WEB_LOG_FORMAT and passes in, and telemetry reads no environment variable itself; plus R75's request-span layer. LEVEL LADDER (F274), one total order, highest first, with every command-line flag above the environment variable as CLI Design Standard R5.1 requires - --debug (TRACE plus internal detail: target, file, line, thread) > --log-level with the values off, error, warn, info, debug and trace > --quiet/-q (ERROR) > -v/-vv/-vvv (INFO/DEBUG/TRACE) > RSLBP_LOG_LEVEL > config-file [logging].level > default WARN; --log-format with the values auto, console and json, plus RSLBP_LOG_FORMAT, selects the render mode by the same deterministic flag-to-environment mapping. STREAMS - every diagnostic byte goes to stderr and stdout is never written by the pipeline, per CLI Design Standard R7.1 and R67's requirement that stdout stays byte-empty on the error path; the pipeline never emits R67's error envelope, which the error boundary owns. EXTENSION INTERFACE - two declared slots with nothing decided in them: a layer slot in telemetry::init where R78's tracing-opentelemetry layer attaches under an otel = ["web", ...] feature nesting on R69's web, with a matching trace_id/span_id serialisation point in the owned FormatEvent, and with W3C traceparent propagation deliberately NOT gated by that feature because REST API Design Standard R11.8 requires it unconditionally on the HTTP surface; and a sink slot where R59's file sink attaches as a second Layer with its own MakeWriter and its own per-layer Filter, which is how a sink gets a level independent of the console.
